scope: Corollary 8.1 (Fixed and minimum energy credits) of the manuscript “Deterministic quasipolynomial-time mean-payoff games” (preprints/Deterministic-quasipolynomial-time-mean-payoff-games-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 104 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5d8d8876fd2982fd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 21. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Uniform deterministic algorithms have the following guarantees. 1. Given v and a nonnegative binary integer c, decide whether (v, c) is energy-winning. On a positive answer, return a positional Max policy satisfying Equation (8.1) from that start and credit against every history-dependent Min strategy. 2. Given v, return the exact cmin(v), including the possible answer ∞. On a finite answer, return a positional Max policy winning from v at credit cmin(v). The fixed-credit computation takes 2O((log2(Lc+2))2) bit operations, where Lc is the full explicit input length including the start and credit. The minimum-credit computation takes 2O((log2(L+2))2) bit operations for the original game length L. Handling every vertex by separate per-start searches, including a separate policy for every finite answer, has the same form of total bit bound. Each policy may depend on the queried start and credit; it also wins from that same start at every larger credit.
